subject.title: [Bug]: sessions_spawn fails with "missing scope: operator.write" from HTTP-mode channel sessions (empty plugin-route runtime scopes)

question: Should trusted internal `sessions_spawn` calls force method-derived synthetic scopes at the subagent chokepoint instead of inheriting a weaker HTTP plugin-route client?
rationale: The narrow repair restores an established workflow, but selecting the authority source is an authorization-boundary decision and must avoid granting write scope to unrelated plugin-route operations.

options.title: Force scope at subagent chokepoint
options.body: Force a synthetic client carrying only the method-derived scope for trusted internal subagent lifecycle calls, with focused HTTP-route regression tests.

options.title: Broaden plugin-route baseline
options.body: Give non-gateway-auth plugin HTTP routes baseline operator scope, affecting every runtime operation initiated from those routes.

options.title: Keep HTTP spawn unsupported
options.body: Preserve the restriction and replace the misleading scope failure with an explicit unsupported-transport error and documentation.

recommendation.title: Force scope at subagent chokepoint
recommendation.body: Force a synthetic client carrying only the method-derived scope for trusted internal subagent lifecycle calls, with focused HTTP-route regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history covers both the central subagent implementation and its security boundaries.
